items.title: Royal Caribbean (RCL) Stock Looks Cheap On Its 178% Five Year Run
items.summary: Royal Caribbean Cruises has delivered a powerful 177.9% share price gain over the past five years, yet the stock is currently down sharply over the last year. This puts fresh attention on whether its earnings still justify where the market is pricing it today. With that mixed return profile and a series of capital and expansion moves underway, the question for readers is how much of the earnings story is already embedded in the valuation. items.title: Is Carnival Stock Cheap, Or Is The Cash Already Spoken For?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) threw off free cash worth 9.7% of its market value over the last twelve months, more than twice the 4.4% median for an S&P 500 company. A yield that high usually means a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Carnival is not that simple. The cash is real, and a large share of it belongs to its lenders.

items.title: Should You Buy Royal Caribbean At A One-Year Low?
items.summary: Royal Caribbean (RCL) trades near $235, at its 52-week low, and over the past year the stock returned about -27% against close to 18% for the S&P 500. The easy read on a cruise line down that far is that demand cracked. It did not. The company lifted its earnings outlook for 2026 and expects adjusted earnings per share to grow 14%, and what has stalled, in the third quarter of 2026, is the price it can put on a cabin.
